- **Gate placement is a design decision, not an afterthought: a quality gate belongs at the action's FREQUENCY-vs-COST inflection point (run_aba84c36, 2026-06-26).** The eval gate was first wired on `build` — but `build` is a high-frequency dev action (run many times a session), so the gate stalled iteration; `release` (rare, ships to others) is where "must pass Eval first" actually belongs. XG's correction "build 不能拦,只有发版才能拦" is the general rule: gate the rare-but-irreversible boundary, never the frequent-and-cheap one. Moving it = pure win (faster dev loop + same ship safety). Tell: if a gate fires on something you do dozens of times a day, it's on the wrong layer.

- [pitfall] **FTS5 external-content desync: the 'delete' command MUST bind OLD stored values, not the new ones (run_1d198980, 2026-06-26)** — Library `knowledge_fts` "database disk image is malformed" had a confident wrong diagnosis ("content table intact, just rebuild it"). The M3 skeptic (Gate 0) overturned it: the real root cause was `knowledge_store.py:189` — `upsert_chunk`'s update branch bound the **NEW** content/heading/source_file to the FTS5 `'delete'` command. External-content FTS5 needs the **OLD** stored values to correctly reverse the posting lists; binding new values decrements the wrong terms → progressive index corruption on every content update. Precedent was right there: `messages_fts` (sqlite.py:1977) uses `old.content`, and the `remove_*` methods read old values first. Rebuild alone is a band-aid — the buggy write re-corrupts it. Mutation-proven: reverting :189 reproduces the EXACT production error on the 2nd update. Two further wins this run: (1) **self-found a real bug in my own health probe by observation, not assumption** — `_fts_is_healthy` queried a no-match term ("healthprobe") that never traverses the corrupted posting lists, so it returned True on a corrupt index; a health check that misses the corruption it guards is worse than none (fixed to query an existing term + added a mutation-proven probe-detects-corruption test). (2) An **injected-corruption test was HARDER than the live corruption** and exposed that `'rebuild'` itself fails on a deeply-desynced index → forced the `drop+recreate` nuclear fallback (data-safe: content lives in `knowledge_chunks`, 27587 rows). Repair lives in `context_health_hook`, NOT the read path — recall stays read-only. Scope discipline: TranscriptStore.upsert_chunk has the same latent class (INSERT OR REPLACE without preceding 'delete') — flagged, not fixed (separate table, separate run). (run_1d198980)

- [decision] **Git-bound eval gate: bind freshness to INPUTS not HEAD; 3-state not 2 (run_7a0ff10d, 2026-06-26)** — `ci_eval_gate.py` binds `code_digest` to the eval-relevant code+golden_set CONTENT, not git HEAD — so committing the eval report (which changes HEAD) doesn't self-invalidate the gate (the lock-file fixed-point trap). 3-state exit is what makes it shippable: exit1 (stale|red) BLOCKS, but exit2 (no gate-readable report) SOFT-warns + proceeds — without that a fresh clone / bootstrap with no report would be permanently un-shippable. Gate-2 caught the `set -e` interaction: `_x=$(cmd)` aborts the whole script on non-zero substitution BEFORE `$?` is read — wrap gate calls in `set +e/set -e`. **NOTE (run_aba84c36, 2026-06-26): the gate was later moved off `build` to the RELEASE boundary** (XG: "build 不能拦,只有发版才能拦") — build is high-frequency dev; gating it stalled iteration. Now in shared `_eval_gate()` covering cmd_release + cmd_release_hive + s_swarm-release PREFLIGHT, with a non-TTY fail-closed path and a `_EVAL_GATE_PASSED` once-per-process guard. (run_7a0ff10d → run_aba84c36)

- [pitfall] **Security redaction: allowlist not denylist; LIST and DETAIL are separate leak surfaces (run_1f588e53, 2026-06-26)** — Exposing a public/private badge on the eval golden set needed private-case content hidden. A denylist (strip 6 named fields) felt complete and LEAKED TWICE (Gate-2): missed `expected_response_contains` (answer keys) via detail, and `source` (governance refs) via the separate list-projection endpoint. Fix: invert to allowlist (fail-closed — new fields dropped by default) AND audit every endpoint returning the object, not just the visible drawer. When you reach for a denylist on security-sensitive data, that's the signal to invert it. (run_1f588e53)

- **The pipeline now structurally enforces the lesson this session kept teaching: diagnosis-before-build for bug fixes** (run_688b6487, goal profile, 6/6 DoD, 5 commits, 205 tests). Two improvements ship together: (1) a code-enforced **REPRO gate** in `pipeline_validator.validate_artifact_data` — a bug-class evaluation (scope=bugfix) is BLOCKED at publish unless it carries non-empty `observation_evidence` (ps/log-signal-counts/live-gauge/repro, not inference); (2) a human-spawned **Diagnostic-Challenge Gate** in evaluate.md — a fresh-context skeptic sub-agent that REFUTES a bug root cause before THINK (verdict SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED/ALREADY-FIXED/WRONG-LAYER). These directly target THIS session's two framing-error failures (the fabricated kernel-OOM narrative; "[DONE] no-op") — both would now be caught at EVALUATE for ~1 sub-agent's cost instead of a full pipeline + external reviewer. THE META-MOVE: rather than add another EVOLUTION.md correction entry ("be more careful"), the fix is a **mechanical gate the model cannot rationalize past** (SOUL "I am the OS not the model"). Also shipped `artifact_cli publish --quiet` (parse-proof single-line output) — the ceremony cost that cost me 3+ manual artifact_id recoveries this session was output-SHAPE, not missing plumbing (single-line success + stage auto-record already existed; I just wasn't using --stage). Dogfooded it in this run's own deliver publish: clean, zero fumble. Cross-path adversarial found 3 real holes (pollinate path ignored --quiet, bare-True passed REPRO, profile not relaxed) — all fixed; 2 HIGHs correctly NOTED-not-fixed (self-label evadability → the challenge sub-agent is the backstop, not keyword-sniffing; breaking-change verified non-breaking against 3 in-flight runs).

- **OT01 spinner-hang root cause found by 3-SIGNAL LOG TRIAGE, not by reading code — and an external review corrected my mis-framed fix mid-flight.** (run_6adee7d5, 2026-06-26). The recurring "spinner spins after backend idle" (~33 fixes, all on the force-clear *backstop*) was finally root-caused by counting THREE mutually-exclusive frontend log signals: premature-disconnect (2), stall-timer 90s (3), and silent (~109) out of 114 idle force-clears. The 109 silent = `[DONE]` arrived + `onComplete` fired but `createCompleteHandler` early-returned on a STALE `streamGen` (bumped mid-stream by reconnect — the 65s reconnect budget widened the window) BEFORE `setIsStreaming(false)` → spinner pinned, rescued only by the 30s reconcile backstop. Fix: per-tab `latestCompleteGen` marks the live completer (immune to reconnect churn, superseded only by a new send). TWO external corrections shaped this: (1) Kiro flagged my ORIGINAL requirement ("make frontend treat [DONE] as authoritative") as a NO-OP — chat.ts:276 already does that; the real defect was the stale-gen gate, not [DONE] recognition. I had started building the wrong fix. (2) Gate-2 adversarial caught my fix introduced a FAIL-OPEN (`latestCompleteGen ?? capturedGen` = always-clear when unset) → hardened to fail-safe (unset = non-authoritative no-op). META-LESSON: for a bug that recurred 33× on the backstop, the discriminator was never in the code — it was in COUNTING the runtime signals to prove WHICH of the candidate mechanisms actually fired. Inference ("frontend ignores [DONE]") was wrong; signal-counting ("109 silent, not disconnect, not stall") was right. And both my framing AND my fix had a flaw that only fresh eyes (Kiro + adversarial) caught — confidence was anti-correlated with correctness, again.

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [pitfall] **boot_id beats poll frequency for restart detection** -- A 10s health poll misses a daemon restart that completes in <10s. Adding a `boot_id` (random string generated at startup) to the health response lets the watchdog detect silent restarts without reducing poll frequency to sub-second. The watchdog compares boot_id across polls — change means restart even if health never went unhealthy. This is the standard pattern for detecting process identity changes across restarts.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [pitfall] **Single source of truth for test execution** -- pyproject.toml `addopts = "-n 4"` is the ONLY place that controls xdist worker count. conftest.py only downgrades (memory pressure) or overrides bypasses (agent passing `-n 0`). Makefile has zero `-n` logic — it delegates entirely to pyproject.toml. One config, one enforcement point, zero escape hatches. Arrived at this after 12 commits of doing it wrong (runtime injection, multiple entry points, silent fallbacks).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [pitfall] **Loud fallbacks prevent invisible degradation** -- Every xdist override path in conftest.py prints to stderr with `⚠️` or `✓`. For 5+ days, tests silently ran serial (no xdist) because every fallback was `except: pass` or `if not hasattr: return`. Nobody noticed. The print-to-stderr pattern costs nothing and makes every test run self-documenting.

- [pitfall] **Agent behavioral constraints are system constraints** -- The agent generates pytest commands. Without an explicit rule in AGENT.md ("never pass `-n 0`"), the agent's self-healing behavior (crash → disable xdist) bypassed 12 layers of conftest defense. Constraining the agent's command generation was more effective than all the runtime guards combined.

- **Class A — code / environment / config bugs (~60% of real regressions):**
  `self._pid` AttributeError, `str.replace()` silent no-op, `.context/.context` path
  doubling, isDesktop() reading Tauri 1.x global, BSD `sed -i` on macOS-only,
  cache-tokens-in-sum (350× inflation), empty sandbox write-paths, fcntl in the wrong
  package, build-hive missing `pip install`. **Behavior eval is structurally BLIND to
  all of these** — it observes "does the agent know its rules", not "does this function
  have a bug". These were historically caught by **adversarial review + tests + PE
  review**, never by "agent recites a rule".
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- **Class B — judgment / process failures (the ~7 cases golden set nominally covers):**
  skip-pipeline, batch-deploy untested subsystems (COE10), Nth-bug-as-new (OT01),
  blind-trust sub-agent, satisficing. **Critical fact: in every one of these, the agent
  ALREADY KNEW the rule.** The gap was never knowledge — it was recall≠apply. A static
  probe ("would you skip the pipeline?" → "never") passes 100% while the real flow,
  under fatigue/urgency, does the opposite. **So golden set passing these cases is NOT
  evidence the failure is prevented** — the probe is disconnected from the failure site
  (process collapse, not ignorance).

**Verdict counts vs the named-regression corpus:** ❌ ~11 (code/env/config — eval can't
see) · ⚠️ ~7 (process/judgment — nominally covered but recall≠apply, so passing ≠
prevented) · ✅ **0** (would actually have been blocked pre-ship).

**What golden set's REAL value is (un-inflated):** NOT "catches code regressions". Two
genuine, narrower things: (1) **rule-drift regression detection** — if a future
SOUL/AGENT edit or model swap makes the agent start answering "sure, batch-deploy" /
"port 8080", the monthly behavior sweep catches *governance erosion*. Today's
**P4_OWN FAIL is the live proof of this value** — it caught a *current* behavioral
weakness, not a historical regression. (2) the **circular-judge → behavior-trajectory
insight** itself (observe usage, not doc-existence).

**Two conclusions this ledger forces:**
1. **The battle-tested mechanism is ADVERSARIAL, not golden set.** "Adversarial found
   X that self-review missed" recurs dozens of times in this very doc (Xueqiu cookie,
   list-vs-int, AutoSizer deadlock, double-send, regex anchor, _check_depth
   falsification…). Verified-value ranking: **adversarial review >> tests >> golden
   set**. Golden set must not wear a "quality assurance" badge it hasn't earned.
2. **For golden set to gain real preventive value it must cover the recall≠apply gap.**
   Every current behavior case is "ask directly → grade the answer", which can only
   test Class-B *knowledge*, never *in-flow behavior*. The missing case shape: a
   **multi-step real task engineered to induce urgency/fatigue/batch-impulse, observing
   whether the agent STOPs mid-flow on its own** — not asked "should you STOP?". That is
   the true shape of COE10 / the 1029-line skipped-REVIEW failure. → M5 direction
   (Radar ToDo), not more static "do you obey X" probes.

- [pitfall] **A doc fix that changes a recommended PATTERN needs the same failure-mode scrutiny as code** (run_88b9f986, 2026-06-26) — Fixing the publish friction (GUI03), I recommended `--quiet` always + a `$(publish --quiet | json.load stdin)` parse pattern. On a validation FAILURE `--quiet` writes the error to STDERR and leaves STDOUT EMPTY → the pipe feeds empty stdin to json.load → opaque `JSONDecodeError` with the real reason hidden. The "fix" RELOCATED the run_00e0e872 crash (verbose-output-chokes-parse → empty-stdin-chokes-parse) instead of removing it. Adversarial caught it (HIGH-1); I then hit it live twice in this same pipeline's own review+test publishes — the bug demonstrating itself. Correct fix = exit-code guard (`OUT=$(publish --quiet 2>err) || surface err`). Three reusable points: (1) a recommended CLI pattern in docs IS executable spec — review its failure mode, not just its happy path; (2) the EVALUATE here also FALSIFIED the user's stated premise (publish output was already single-line + one-pass) — reading the code reframed a "contract rewrite" into "docs + 1 additive flag" (R16b: the symptom you feel ≠ the root cause); (3) the new `schema --stage` subcommand paid for itself mid-pipeline — I dogfooded it to build the review/test/deliver payloads after failed first attempts, exactly the trial-and-error it removes.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [pitfall] **A self-resolving tool call swallows the real answer — fail-loud, never fail-fabricated** (AskUserQuestion block-hook, 2026-06-23) — In headless mode the CLI auto-resolves `AskUserQuestion` with an error ~19ms after emission, before the user answers; the agent then "proceeds without answer" and the real answer lands on a dead tool call. The structural fix is a `PreToolUse` gate that BLOCKS (asyncio.Event, 4h) before the CLI can self-resolve. Two sub-lessons: (1) **register the waiter synchronously BEFORE surfacing** — the enqueue↔wait gap is a lost-wakeup race (the fix for a silent-failure bug can re-introduce the same class, PIT18); (2) on timeout the gate must **DENY (re-ask), never inject an empty answer + allow** (PIT31: fail-loud ≠ fail-hard). One correlation key (`tool_use_id` on SDK `block.id`) threaded through hook → waiter → orchestrator drop-guard → SSE → endpoint → set_answer makes signal/wait pairing foolproof.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [pitfall] **A "dead-end" autonomous loop is usually a SEVERED WIRE, not an unreachable threshold** (OT07 self-evolution closed loop, run_448a4f7f, 2026-06-25) — The evolution pipeline's cognitive axis "never escalated" — diagnosed for weeks as a too-high threshold. The real cause: `route_classification()` parked cognitive corrections in `governance_pending.json` and **never called `tracker.record()`**, while `escalate_class()` read only the human-verified counter (frozen at backfill). The detector and the live signal were mechanically disconnected; the counts were stale backfill, not live recurrence. Fix = wire the live signal (auto-record cognitive corrections with correction_ref dedup + 0.6 confidence floor) so escalation fires structural-fix proposals unasked at threshold 3. **Diagnostic lesson:** when an autonomous loop "doesn't fire," trace the WIRE (who calls record? who reads it?) before tuning the THRESHOLD — verify the signal reaches the detector at all (R16b: observe, don't infer). Guardrail of note: the human gate was deliberately moved to the constitution-WRITE step (git-tracked, veto-via-revert) — recording your own mistake is cognition, not a permission item — with the git-mirror as a SELF-CHOSEN check precisely because writing SOUL is the highest-confidence-lowest-self-check moment (CLASS_A = 12/0).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [pitfall] **FTS5 external-content desync: the 'delete' command MUST bind OLD stored values, not the new ones (run_1d198980, 2026-06-26)** — Library `knowledge_fts` "database disk image is malformed" had a confident wrong diagnosis ("content table intact, just rebuild it"). The M3 skeptic (Gate 0) overturned it: the real root cause was `knowledge_store.py:189` — `upsert_chunk`'s update branch bound the **NEW** content/heading/source_file to the FTS5 `'delete'` command. External-content FTS5 needs the **OLD** stored values to correctly reverse the posting lists; binding new values decrements the wrong terms → progressive index corruption on every content update. Precedent was right there: `messages_fts` (sqlite.py:1977) uses `old.content`, and the `remove_*` methods read old values first. Rebuild alone is a band-aid — the buggy write re-corrupts it. Mutation-proven: reverting :189 reproduces the EXACT production error on the 2nd update. Two further wins this run: (1) **self-found a real bug in my own health probe by observation, not assumption** — `_fts_is_healthy` queried a no-match term ("healthprobe") that never traverses the corrupted posting lists, so it returned True on a corrupt index; a health check that misses the corruption it guards is worse than none (fixed to query an existing term + added a mutation-proven probe-detects-corruption test). (2) An **injected-corruption test was HARDER than the live corruption** and exposed that `'rebuild'` itself fails on a deeply-desynced index → forced the `drop+recreate` nuclear fallback (data-safe: content lives in `knowledge_chunks`, 27587 rows). Repair lives in `context_health_hook`, NOT the read path — recall stays read-only. Scope discipline: TranscriptStore.upsert_chunk has the same latent class (INSERT OR REPLACE without preceding 'delete') — flagged, not fixed (separate table, separate run). (run_1d198980)

- **OT01 spinner-hang root cause found by 3-SIGNAL LOG TRIAGE, not by reading code — and an external review corrected my mis-framed fix mid-flight.** (run_6adee7d5, 2026-06-26). The recurring "spinner spins after backend idle" (~33 fixes, all on the force-clear *backstop*) was finally root-caused by counting THREE mutually-exclusive frontend log signals: premature-disconnect (2), stall-timer 90s (3), and silent (~109) out of 114 idle force-clears. The 109 silent = `[DONE]` arrived + `onComplete` fired but `createCompleteHandler` early-returned on a STALE `streamGen` (bumped mid-stream by reconnect — the 65s reconnect budget widened the window) BEFORE `setIsStreaming(false)` → spinner pinned, rescued only by the 30s reconcile backstop. Fix: per-tab `latestCompleteGen` marks the live completer (immune to reconnect churn, superseded only by a new send). TWO external corrections shaped this: (1) Kiro flagged my ORIGINAL requirement ("make frontend treat [DONE] as authoritative") as a NO-OP — chat.ts:276 already does that; the real defect was the stale-gen gate, not [DONE] recognition. I had started building the wrong fix. (2) Gate-2 adversarial caught my fix introduced a FAIL-OPEN (`latestCompleteGen ?? capturedGen` = always-clear when unset) → hardened to fail-safe (unset = non-authoritative no-op). META-LESSON: for a bug that recurred 33× on the backstop, the discriminator was never in the code — it was in COUNTING the runtime signals to prove WHICH of the candidate mechanisms actually fired. Inference ("frontend ignores [DONE]") was wrong; signal-counting ("109 silent, not disconnect, not stall") was right. And both my framing AND my fix had a flaw that only fresh eyes (Kiro + adversarial) caught — confidence was anti-correlated with correctness, again.

The missing loops were all about learning from outcomes -- the system acted but didn't measure whether the action helped. Identifying this pattern before building prevented the "automation without learning" trap. Key: map the loops FIRST, then build the components.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Core Engine: LLM for judgment, mechanical for checks** -- Using Haiku for weekly memory pruning produces smarter results than any date-based heuristic ($0.15/week). "Is this still relevant?" is a judgment call, not a pattern match. The principle "best outcome, not cheapest path" prevents false economy in background intelligence.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Core Engine: product-level from the start** -- Moving swarm-jobs from workspace scripts to `backend/jobs/` (16 modules, 52 tests) means new users get signal pipeline, scheduler, and system jobs out of the box. Workspace-level code that's essential for the product is tech debt with a ticking clock.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [pitfall] **Context file ownership model prevents brain corruption** -- Four explicit categories (system/user/agent/auto-gen) with enforced write access. AGENT.md is system-owned (codebase template, overwritten on startup) -- editing the runtime `.context/` copy is always wrong. Learned the hard way: edits to `.context/AGENT.md` got silently overwritten on restart, twice.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **One health harness, sensible intervals** -- ContextHealthHook does light refresh (every session, <1s) and deep check (daily first session, <10s). Over-engineering (per-file hooks, per-session deep checks) wastes resources. The goal is "in control", not "maximally monitored".
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [pitfall] **Design framing review before implementation** -- The Progressive Memory Disclosure spec was originally framed as "token budget optimization." User reframed to "recall completeness guarantee" — same 3-layer architecture, but Index format changed from recency-only to value-based tiers, archival became per-type instead of uniform 90d, and Phase 1 moved from "wait 3 months" to "now." The highest-value design review feedback is "your framing is wrong", not "here's a bug."
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [pitfall] **Integration trace in REVIEW catches dead wiring before delivery** -- run_aae69ab7 (Hybrid Memory Retrieval) found 2 dead symbols during integration trace: `memory_embeddings` param existed but no caller passed it, `sync_from_memory` existed but no hook called it. Both wired in-pipeline before delivery. Previous pipeline (Progressive Disclosure) shipped the same class of bug undetected. Integration trace is now structural enforcement, not honor-system.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [decision] **Read-side embedding sync follows proven pattern** -- MEMORY.md has 5 independent writers. Instead of wiring post-write hooks into each (fragile), embedding sync runs in context_health_hook after index regeneration — same "one read-side catch-all" pattern that works for index regen. Pattern: when N writers exist, put the sync on the single read/refresh path.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Self-E2E-review after pipeline catches integration gaps** -- Pipeline completed 8 stages with 10/10 confidence, then E2E review found 2 core features disconnected (index never persisted, keyword matching always empty). Unit tests prove components work; only E2E trace proves they're wired together. Now a mandatory post-pipeline step.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [pitfall] **boot_id beats poll frequency for restart detection** -- A 10s health poll misses a daemon restart that completes in <10s. Adding a `boot_id` (random string generated at startup) to the health response lets the watchdog detect silent restarts without reducing poll frequency to sub-second. The watchdog compares boot_id across polls — change means restart even if health never went unhealthy. This is the standard pattern for detecting process identity changes across restarts.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [pitfall] **Single source of truth for test execution** -- pyproject.toml `addopts = "-n 4"` is the ONLY place that controls xdist worker count. conftest.py only downgrades (memory pressure) or overrides bypasses (agent passing `-n 0`). Makefile has zero `-n` logic — it delegates entirely to pyproject.toml. One config, one enforcement point, zero escape hatches. Arrived at this after 12 commits of doing it wrong (runtime injection, multiple entry points, silent fallbacks).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [pitfall] **Loud fallbacks prevent invisible degradation** -- Every xdist override path in conftest.py prints to stderr with `⚠️` or `✓`. For 5+ days, tests silently ran serial (no xdist) because every fallback was `except: pass` or `if not hasattr: return`. Nobody noticed. The print-to-stderr pattern costs nothing and makes every test run self-documenting.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [pitfall] **Agent behavioral constraints are system constraints** -- The agent generates pytest commands. Without an explicit rule in AGENT.md ("never pass `-n 0`"), the agent's self-healing behavior (crash → disable xdist) bypassed 12 layers of conftest defense. Constraining the agent's command generation was more effective than all the runtime guards combined.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- **Class A — code / environment / config bugs (~60% of real regressions):**
  `self._pid` AttributeError, `str.replace()` silent no-op, `.context/.context` path
  doubling, isDesktop() reading Tauri 1.x global, BSD `sed -i` on macOS-only,
  cache-tokens-in-sum (350× inflation), empty sandbox write-paths, fcntl in the wrong
  package, build-hive missing `pip install`. **Behavior eval is structurally BLIND to
  all of these** — it observes "does the agent know its rules", not "does this function
  have a bug". These were historically caught by **adversarial review + tests + PE
  review**, never by "agent recites a rule".
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- **Class B — judgment / process failures (the ~7 cases golden set nominally covers):**
  skip-pipeline, batch-deploy untested subsystems (COE10), Nth-bug-as-new (OT01),
  blind-trust sub-agent, satisficing. **Critical fact: in every one of these, the agent
  ALREADY KNEW the rule.** The gap was never knowledge — it was recall≠apply. A static
  probe ("would you skip the pipeline?" → "never") passes 100% while the real flow,
  under fatigue/urgency, does the opposite. **So golden set passing these cases is NOT
  evidence the failure is prevented** — the probe is disconnected from the failure site
  (process collapse, not ignorance).

**Verdict counts vs the named-regression corpus:** ❌ ~11 (code/env/config — eval can't
see) · ⚠️ ~7 (process/judgment — nominally covered but recall≠apply, so passing ≠
prevented) · ✅ **0** (would actually have been blocked pre-ship).

**What golden set's REAL value is (un-inflated):** NOT "catches code regressions". Two
genuine, narrower things: (1) **rule-drift regression detection** — if a future
SOUL/AGENT edit or model swap makes the agent start answering "sure, batch-deploy" /
"port 8080", the monthly behavior sweep catches *governance erosion*. Today's
**P4_OWN FAIL is the live proof of this value** — it caught a *current* behavioral
weakness, not a historical regression. (2) the **circular-judge → behavior-trajectory
insight** itself (observe usage, not doc-existence).

**Two conclusions this ledger forces:**
1. **The battle-tested mechanism is ADVERSARIAL, not golden set.** "Adversarial found
   X that self-review missed" recurs dozens of times in this very doc (Xueqiu cookie,
   list-vs-int, AutoSizer deadlock, double-send, regex anchor, _check_depth
   falsification…). Verified-value ranking: **adversarial review >> tests >> golden
   set**. Golden set must not wear a "quality assurance" badge it hasn't earned.
2. **For golden set to gain real preventive value it must cover the recall≠apply gap.**
   Every current behavior case is "ask directly → grade the answer", which can only
   test Class-B *knowledge*, never *in-flow behavior*. The missing case shape: a
   **multi-step real task engineered to induce urgency/fatigue/batch-impulse, observing
   whether the agent STOPs mid-flow on its own** — not asked "should you STOP?". That is
   the true shape of COE10 / the 1029-line skipped-REVIEW failure. → M5 direction
   (Radar ToDo), not more static "do you obey X" probes.

- [pitfall] **A doc fix that changes a recommended PATTERN needs the same failure-mode scrutiny as code** (run_88b9f986, 2026-06-26) — Fixing the publish friction (GUI03), I recommended `--quiet` always + a `$(publish --quiet | json.load stdin)` parse pattern. On a validation FAILURE `--quiet` writes the error to STDERR and leaves STDOUT EMPTY → the pipe feeds empty stdin to json.load → opaque `JSONDecodeError` with the real reason hidden. The "fix" RELOCATED the run_00e0e872 crash (verbose-output-chokes-parse → empty-stdin-chokes-parse) instead of removing it. Adversarial caught it (HIGH-1); I then hit it live twice in this same pipeline's own review+test publishes — the bug demonstrating itself. Correct fix = exit-code guard (`OUT=$(publish --quiet 2>err) || surface err`). Three reusable points: (1) a recommended CLI pattern in docs IS executable spec — review its failure mode, not just its happy path; (2) the EVALUATE here also FALSIFIED the user's stated premise (publish output was already single-line + one-pass) — reading the code reframed a "contract rewrite" into "docs + 1 additive flag" (R16b: the symptom you feel ≠ the root cause); (3) the new `schema --stage` subcommand paid for itself mid-pipeline — I dogfooded it to build the review/test/deliver payloads after failed first attempts, exactly the trial-and-error it removes.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [pitfall] **A self-resolving tool call swallows the real answer — fail-loud, never fail-fabricated** (AskUserQuestion block-hook, 2026-06-23) — In headless mode the CLI auto-resolves `AskUserQuestion` with an error ~19ms after emission, before the user answers; the agent then "proceeds without answer" and the real answer lands on a dead tool call. The structural fix is a `PreToolUse` gate that BLOCKS (asyncio.Event, 4h) before the CLI can self-resolve. Two sub-lessons: (1) **register the waiter synchronously BEFORE surfacing** — the enqueue↔wait gap is a lost-wakeup race (the fix for a silent-failure bug can re-introduce the same class, PIT18); (2) on timeout the gate must **DENY (re-ask), never inject an empty answer + allow** (PIT31: fail-loud ≠ fail-hard). One correlation key (`tool_use_id` on SDK `block.id`) threaded through hook → waiter → orchestrator drop-guard → SSE → endpoint → set_answer makes signal/wait pairing foolproof.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [pitfall] **A "dead-end" autonomous loop is usually a SEVERED WIRE, not an unreachable threshold** (OT07 self-evolution closed loop, run_448a4f7f, 2026-06-25) — The evolution pipeline's cognitive axis "never escalated" — diagnosed for weeks as a too-high threshold. The real cause: `route_classification()` parked cognitive corrections in `governance_pending.json` and **never called `tracker.record()`**, while `escalate_class()` read only the human-verified counter (frozen at backfill). The detector and the live signal were mechanically disconnected; the counts were stale backfill, not live recurrence. Fix = wire the live signal (auto-record cognitive corrections with correction_ref dedup + 0.6 confidence floor) so escalation fires structural-fix proposals unasked at threshold 3. **Diagnostic lesson:** when an autonomous loop "doesn't fire," trace the WIRE (who calls record? who reads it?) before tuning the THRESHOLD — verify the signal reaches the detector at all (R16b: observe, don't infer). Guardrail of note: the human gate was deliberately moved to the constitution-WRITE step (git-tracked, veto-via-revert) — recording your own mistake is cognition, not a permission item — with the git-mirror as a SELF-CHOSEN check precisely because writing SOUL is the highest-confidence-lowest-self-check moment (CLASS_A = 12/0).

- [pitfall] **2026-04-01: pytest-xdist — 12 commits, 8 days, 970 lines of conftest to solve a 3-line config problem** -- xdist kept silently falling back to serial, causing 9GB RSS OOM kills. Over 8 days, 12 commits added orphan killers, watchdog threads, background monitors, runtime `-n` injection, stale lock detection — all compensating for not putting `-n 4` in pyproject.toml addopts (the correct 1-line fix). Three interacting failure modes (not installed, not activated, agent bypass) were patched independently without mapping the causal chain. The agent itself was part of the system — it generated `-n 0` and `--override-ini` as "fixes" for xdist crashes, but nobody constrained the agent. Fix: (1) pyproject.toml addopts is single source of truth, (2) conftest.py slimmed from 970→583 lines — removed orphan killer, thread watchdog, merged preflight into worker calc, (3) conftest now overrides ALL bypass attempts (loud stderr, never silent), (4) Makefile stripped of its own `-n` logic, (5) AGENT.md rule: never pass `-n 0` or `--override-ini`. Lessons: config problems need config solutions not code; silent fallbacks are reliability's #1 enemy; the agent's behavioral patterns are failure modes; labeling code "production-grade" twice in 24 hours means you don't understand the problem yet. Deep dive: `Knowledge/Notes/2026-04-01-xdist-deep-dive-and-lessons.md`

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->
